To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Heavy drinking is a major cause of drunken driving.
1) 40% of drunken drivers above 30 years of age had elevated GGT indicating heavy drinking, and 2) 63% of the drivers with a BAC above 55 mm/l (250 mg/%) had elevated GGT.
Heavy drinking is common among Norwegian drunken drivers, particularly in older drivers with high BACs and among drivers with a history of previous arrests for drunk driving.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effects of alcohol on the central nervous system.
the study of the relationship of heavy drinking and drunken driving in Norway.
the development of new methods for the detection of alcohol and other drugs in body fluids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GGT activity is a sensitive and reliable indicator of heavy drinking in the population, and that the GGT method is a useful tool for identifying heavy drinkers among drunken drivers.

a substantial proportion of the drunken drivers are heavy drinkers.
the majority of the drivers with high BACs (above 250 mg/100ml) were heavy drinkers, and that a substantial proportion of the drivers below 29 years of old were not heavy drinkers.

the use of GGT in a population of apprehended drunk drivers may be a useful tool for identifying heavy drinkers.
